acceptance: replay.py and run.py take the disabledRules lines from one shared function.
A test fails if either overlay omits a rule file present in a stand-in rules directory.
One smoke replay of a turn that edits a .py file shows no 'TTSR matched rule' in its output, with the user's code-first rule installed.
The PR lists every other overlay builder in evals/ablation and what was done for each.
description: Problem: run.py lists every file in ~/.omp/agent/rules under ttsr.disabledRules in its sandbox overlay, so a user rule cannot change an evaluation arm. replay.py builds its own overlay and does not. The code-first rule is now installed, so any replay that edits a source file would get the injected reminder in every arm. Outcome: replay sessions disable user rule files exactly as run.py sessions do, from one shared piece of code. Decision gate: none; this is a defect fix. If any other session launcher in evals/ablation builds its own overlay (the loading-map probe, isolation_probe.py), list it in the PR and apply the same fix or state why it is not needed. Guardrails: no change to what replay.py writes into results or to scenario and check hashes; no edits to the user's rules directory; do not run a replay against a real session's original files other than through replay.py's own copy; verify with one smoke replay costing under 2 USD; publish by task branch and draft PR as Joe Harris <joeharris76@gmail.com>, and the item stays open until merged.
